posts.text:
I had a good and productive meeting with UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting @wesstreeting in Kyiv. Thank you for this visit on the Day of Dignity and Freedom, of all days. Being here with our people at a time when Russia is launching brutal, massive strikes every day and every night sends a strong signal to the aggressor that support for Ukraine will not diminish. I thanked the United Kingdom for its new defense and humanitarian packages – worth more than £500 million in total. This is a very tangible boost to our defenses, and it is important that the UK is leading by example in its support for Ukraine.

We discussed specific defense capabilities Ukraine needs right now. Above all, air defense to protect our energy infrastructure, logistics, water supply, and other things that keep life in Kyiv and the regions normal. The UK does not have its own Patriot missiles, but it has strong ties across Europe and around the world that can help find the anti-ballistic missiles we need. We are counting on this. We also talked about joint production and long-range capabilities. Together, we can significantly strengthen Ukraine’s missile program. Of course, we also discussed Russia’s escalation against Europe, including the Russian missile that flew into Poland, where the Coalition of the Willing was holding exercises at the time. A strong European response to this Russian brazenness is needed, along with greater pressure.

I thank Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the Government, and the people of Britain for their unwavering support.

And it’s all about Jinggangshan — the mountains where the Red Army was born.
